about.title: Solvang Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Solvang is small enough that a death touches nearly everyone. With about 5,741 residents, a family's loss here is felt along Mission Drive and Rt 246, and out on Alamo Pintado Road and Fredensborg Canyon Road, where much of the town's daily driving happens. In 2025, public records show 15 injury collisions and 21 people hurt in Solvang, and no traffic deaths were recorded that year. Still, wrongful death claims in Santa Barbara County arise from more than roadways: a fall at a rental property, a medical error, a defective product, or a workplace incident can all take a life that should not have been lost. California law lets a spouse or domestic partner and children bring the claim first, followed by certain dependents and heirs. The deadline is generally two years from the date of death, and it is shorter when a public agency is involved. LawProactive is not a law firm. We simply connect you, at no cost, with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency.

items.title: Standing Is Checked Early
items.desc: California limits who may bring a wrongful death action, starting with a spouse or domestic partner and children, then certain dependents and heirs. The attorney you are connected with sorts this out at the start so the right people are part of the claim.

items.desc: You generally have two years from the date of death to file, and far less time when a city, county, or state agency may share fault. Getting connected promptly protects those windows.

items.question: Solvang had no traffic deaths in 2025. Does that mean wrongful death claims are rare here?
items.answer: Fatal collisions are only one source of these claims. In a town like Solvang, where reported crashes tend to cluster on Saturday afternoons between 4 p.m. and 6 p.m. on corridors like Mission Drive and Rt 246, the risk on the road is real, but deaths from medical negligence, unsafe property, or defective products happen quietly and are just as actionable. Any death caused by someone else's carelessness can be reviewed by an attorney.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death lawsuit in California?
items.answer: The law gives first priority to the surviving spouse or registered domestic partner and the children of the person who died. If there is no one in that group, certain dependents and heirs may qualify instead. Because the list is specific, it helps to have an attorney confirm who has standing before anything is filed.

items.question: If the other person is being prosecuted, do we still need a civil case?
items.answer: Yes, the two are separate. A criminal case is brought by the government and can end in penalties for the defendant, but it does not compensate your family. A wrongful death action is a civil claim that seeks payment for funeral costs, lost financial support, and the loss of love and guidance, and it moves forward on its own two-year clock regardless of what happens in criminal court.
